title: Tried building a survivors-like with MiniMax M3.1 Flash, here's the game in demo mode
author: CuteRole7793
selftext:
You're watching a survivors-like play itself in demo mode, nobody at the keyboard. It came from one prompt to MiniMax's M3.1 Flash in OpenCode (max variant): auto-attacks, waves, bosses, XP, a level-up screen, and that self-playing demo. Didn't touch the file after.

What came back: "Neon Survivors," about 2,500 lines of self-contained HTML. 8 weapons, 6 enemy types, bosses every 2 minutes, screen shake, hit-stop, damage numbers, and a combo counter. The title screen runs a full AI demo where the game picks its own upgrades and starts a new run when it dies. The video is 15 seconds of that.

It installed a headless browser while building and play-tested the game in it, including a stress test with a big wave of enemies. The run took 90 minutes and cost about 25 cents.

How far do you push single-prompt runs before you start iterating?

comments.author: Mason-Green41
comments.body: how well does the generated code hold up when u start adding new mechanics or changing existing ones?
